name: Blonde Redhead
label: 4AD
lede: A Japanese art student and two Italian jazz-school twins took their name from a no wave song, made five noisy records for Smells Like and Touch and Go, then remade themselves on 4AD after a horse nearly took Kazu Makino's face.

eras.title: Named for a DNA song
eras.text: New York's downtown noise scene was still loud in 1993, and Arto Lindsay's old band supplied the name. The twins and Makino started as a four-piece and cut their first two albums for Steve Shelley's label in under two years.

years.h: Two Pace twins meet a film student in Manhattan
years.p: Amedeo and Simone Pace, born in Milan and raised in Montreal, came to New York after jazz studies in Boston. Kazu Makino was studying film. Maki Takahashi played bass.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says they met through mutual friends; John Lurie wrote in his memoir that he introduced the twins to Makino, a longtime friend. The name came from "Blonde Redhead" on the 1981 EP A Taste of DNA by the no wave band [[DNA|97cecdca-af46-4344-9677-ed80bfe43b66]].

For the band's first decade, Amedeo Pace and Makino were also a couple.

years.h: "Amescream" b/w "Big Song": the first 7-inch
years.p: The debut single comes out in 1993, a year before any album. "Vague" b/w "Jet Star" follows in 1994.

years.src: Wikipedia: Blonde Redhead · Los Angeles Times
years.h: Sonic Youth's drummer produces the debut, on his own label
years.p: [[Steve Shelley|998815d5-03bc-4228-807f-b550c07038d2]] of [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] produces Blonde Redhead and puts it out on Smells Like Records as SLR-007.

years.h: Takahashi leaves, and her friend Toko Yasuda takes the bass
years.p: Maki Takahashi quits soon after the debut. Toko Yasuda plays on the second album and is gone by the next one, leaving the trio that has lasted ever since.

years.h: La Mia Vita Violenta, the second Smells Like album in a year
years.p: An Italian title for a New York noise record, with "10 Feet High" and "Valentine" pulled as a single.

eras.title: Three records in Chicago's orbit
eras.text: Touch and Go gave the trio a home among the labels that mattered to noise rock, and Fugazi's Guy Picciotto came aboard as producer. By 2000 the songs were quieter and more personal, and the money was tight.

years.cap: Kazu Makino with Amedeo and Simone Pace as a trio, c. 1997
years.h: Touch and Go signs the trio, and Unwound's bassist sits in
years.p: The first of three Touch and Go albums. With no bass player of their own, they borrow [[Vern Rumsey|a4d62ca9-11fa-4658-90a7-71317f8f37d0]] of [[Unwound|9434776a-bdd7-4f58-b719-b5d95b9d2a11]].
years.xp: Later records used the Icelandic bassist Skúli Sverrisson. The 1997 single paired "Symphony of Treble" with "Kasuality".

years.h: Guy Picciotto of Fugazi takes the producer's chair
years.p: [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] produces the fourth album, helps build "Futurism vs. Passéism Part 2" and sings on it.
play: In an Expression of the Inexpressible

years.h: A record about the couple inside the band
years.p: Picciotto and Ryan Hadlock co-produce. Wikipedia describes the album as being about Makino and Amedeo Pace's relationship.
years.xp:
It closes with "For the Damaged Coda", an instrumental that later reached 15 on Billboard's Hot Rock and Alternative Songs chart.

A companion EP, Mélodie Citronique, also came out on Touch and Go in 2000.

years.big: "My only thought was 'How can we play?'"
q: I was just struggling to write good songs.
years.h: Thrown from a horse, Makino has her jaw wired shut
years.p: The horse trampled her jaw and crushed facial bones that needed major reconstructive surgery, the Los Angeles Times reported. She asked Amedeo Pace to sing her songs so shows wouldn't be cancelled.
years.xp:
Makino told the Times the pain wasn't the worst part: "I wasn't even sad or suffering. I was just struggling to write good songs."

Recovery took months. "When I got the wires out I thought I could just bite into an apple," she said. When she finally ate one, "I think I cried." The sleeve of the next album thanks her surgeons for "putting her back in one piece".

eras.title: Paying for it themselves
eras.text: The trio left Touch and Go, paid for a record out of their own pockets and only then went looking for a label. 4AD took it, and the noise gave way to something closer to the label's own history.

years.h: Out of Touch and Go, the band funds its own album
years.p: Simone Pace said they wanted no limits on expenses: "with Touch & Go, sometimes things were a little tight." They recorded with Picciotto at Rare Book Room in New York with no label behind them.

years.src: Poetic Wax · Los Angeles Times · Wikipedia: Blonde Redhead
years.h: Misery Is a Butterfly lands on 4AD
years.p: Picciotto's last production for them. "Elephant Woman" and "Equus" circle the accident, though Makino has said the album isn't about it.
years.xp:
Amedeo Pace told the Guardian the band was deep in French music and soundtracks while everyone else was playing garage rock and dance punk. Makino said she hated the album the moment it was finished.

"Elephant Woman" reached 82 on the UK singles chart and "Equus" 84, the band's only UK chart singles.

years.h: The Secret Society of Butterflies EP on 4AD and Beggars Banquet
years.p: A stopgap EP between Misery and the next album.

years.cap: Blonde Redhead at Villa Ada, Rome, June 2007
years.src: Los Angeles Times · Wikipedia: Blonde Redhead
years.h: Alan Moulder mixes 23, and some old fans balk
years.p: Their most song-shaped record reaches 63 in the US and 13 on the UK indie chart. The Los Angeles Times noted longtime fans complaining about the missing rough edges.
years.xp: Makino told the Times she sometimes felt the band "could have done better or deserve more," comparing herself to festival headliners like [[Muse|9c9f1380-2516-4fc9-a3e6-f9f61941d090]]: "I just hope we can be better at what we do; I don't wish we were like Muse."

years.cap: Blonde Redhead live in Florence, November 2007
years.h: The 23 tour reaches Florence
years.p: The tour behind 23 reaches Italy. Live, the LA Times wrote, the band barely spoke to the crowd while Makino thrashed behind her hair.

years.h: A score for a documentary about role-players
years.p: The trio writes and records the music for The Dungeon Masters, which premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival.

eras.title: From 4AD to self-financed again
eras.text: Two more years on 4AD brought the band's best US chart showing. Then they made the next album without the label's support, and a cartoon dug up a fourteen-year-old instrumental.

years.h: "When the Road Runs Out" on the Dark Was the Night benefit
years.p: A collaboration with Devastations for the Red Hot Organization's AIDS benefit compilation, which also carries [[Bon Iver|437a0e49-c6ae-42f6-a6c1-84f25ed366bc]].

years.h: "Not Getting There" turns up on a 4AD sampler
years.p: A demo version appears on Fragments From Work In Progress, six months before the album it belongs to.

years.h: Penny Sparkle reaches 79 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Moulder mixes again, and the band adds a keyboard player for the tour.

years.cap: Blonde Redhead at the Festival de musique emergente, Rouyn-Noranda, Quebec
years.h: No 4AD this time: producer Drew Brown and analog only
years.p: The band starts its next record self-financed, with Drew Brown pushing them onto analog instruments.
years.xp: Simone Pace on Brown: "he has so much experience and definitely dictated the direction of the record; the choices of instruments, concept and that it was minimal."

years.cap: Kazu Makino at the Sunset Junction street fair, Los Angeles
years.h: Rick and Morty plays "For the Damaged Coda"
years.p: The 2000 instrumental runs in a first-season episode, comes back in season three as the theme of Evil Morty, and by 2018 is a meme for life's worst moments.

years.h: Barragán comes out on Kobalt
years.p: The ninth album, previewed by "No More Honey" in June and "Dripping" after.

eras.title: Tool, a cartoon and dinner
eras.text: The archive came out first, then a solo record, then an arena tour opening for Tool. Nine years after Barragán, the trio came back with a record about loss.

years.cap: Blonde Redhead and ACME play Misery Is a Butterfly at the Co-Cathedral of St. Joseph, Brooklyn, October 2016
years.src: Bandcamp: Masculin Féminin · Wikipedia: Blonde Redhead
years.h: Numero Group boxes up the Smells Like years
years.p: Masculin Féminin gathers the first two albums, singles, demos and radio sessions: 37 tracks with two essays.

years.h: Makino goes solo with Ryuichi Sakamoto on Adult Baby
years.p: Her first solo album as KAZU, with Ryuichi Sakamoto on piano and [[Greg Saunier|2ae4e9b4-9e8b-4a98-920d-4f3a881dac96]] among the drummers.

years.h: Maynard James Keenan picks them to open for Tool
years.p: A month of US arena dates, from January 10 to February 10. Tool hand-picks its openers.

years.big: "You don't need to get along as people to have strong musical chemistry"
q: You don't need to get along as people to have strong musical chemistry
years.src: Guitar World · Wikipedia: Sit Down for Dinner
years.h: Sit Down for Dinner, the first album in nine years
years.p: Written from 2018, with Joan Didion's The Year of Magical Thinking in the background. Metacritic: 82.
years.xp:
Makino told Guitar World she had been "quite aggressively chasing some kind of independence" in the writing, and that "Kiss Her Kiss Her" stayed with her because of a feeling of "falling behind" Amedeo Pace while writing it in a different country.

Pace's take: "We were all over the place, and dragged through a pandemic, so for this to be as good as it is, it was like we found our voice." In November they cut "More Coda" for Rick and Morty.

years.h: Melbourne's RISING festival, three decades in
years.p: The trio plays the Forum Melbourne on the Sit Down for Dinner run, with Melbourne singer Georgia Knight opening.

years.cap: Blonde Redhead at MGM Music Hall at Fenway, Boston
years.h: "Blood Spilled" arrives as a standalone single
years.p: It follows The Shadow of the Guest, a 2025 compilation on section1.
